text:
A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet. Everything you send goes through it scrambled, so your internet provider or public Wi-Fi can't read it.

The websites you visit see the VPN's address instead of yours, so your location and identity are harder to trace. The catch: you now trust the VPN company with what you used to show your provider.

It helps on public Wi-Fi and for privacy from your provider. It doesn't make you anonymous or protect you from scams and bad downloads.
